newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-FRANCE'S AMIEZ LEAVES TOMBA TRAILING.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-FRANCE'S AMIEZ LEAVES TOMBA TRAILING.

text.p: France's Sebastien Amiez led after the first leg of the men's slalom on Saturday and left Alberto Tomba plenty of work if he is to retain his Alpine skiing world championship title.
Amiez, who has not won a slalom this season but has finished second once and third three times, twisted his way down the floodlit 67-gate Kandahar course in 54.71 seconds.
Amiez, the reigning World Cup slalom champion, carried a healthy 1.02 second advantage over his nearest challenger, Austria's Thomas Sykora, into the second leg.
Sykora, who has dominated the event this season winning five of eight races, clocked 55.73 while Norway's Tom Stiansen was third-quickest in 55.81.
Austrians occupied three of the top five positions as Olympic champion Thomas Stangassinger set the fourth-best time of 55.92 followed closely by compatriot Mario Reiter with 55.93.

"I was a lot slower than Amiez on the lower part of the course," said Sykora, who was forced to wait before pushing out of the start hut because of blustery conditions. "But anything can happen on the second run.
"I could get nothing or I could get gold, silver or bronze -- let's wait and see."
Tomba, first man out of the start hut, brought to life the thousands of fans lining the course and some even hanging from the floodlight pylons.
The crowd, the largest of the championships, cheered their hero's every move and waved signs, one of which read: 'Tomba you are immortal'.
But the flamboyant Italian's first leg time proved that he is all too human. The triple Olympic gold medallist crossed seventh in 56.21, leaving him 1.50 seconds off the pace.
Amiez followed immediately after Tomba and the crowd suddenly fell silent at the gulf between them.

Tomba's succesful arrival in the finish area marked the departure of much of the crowd who, having seen what they had come to see on a freezing evening, headed to bars and restaurants to warm up before the second run at 2000 GMT.
The slalom is the last race of the world championships and also Tomba's last chance of a medal in Italy.
Winner of the slalom and giant slalom titles last year, he failed to finish the giant on Wednesday.
